source.title: How Spurious Features are Memorized: Precise Analysis for Random and NTK Features

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures memorization of label-uncorrelated spurious input features and reports spurious accuracy. This is related to memorization in the claim, but it does not test any listed version about random labels, unstructured inputs, label noise, regularization, or learning order.
record.gate_note: The paper's own results measure predictions on inputs retaining a training sample's spurious feature while replacing its core feature. It does not report results from random-label training or the other version-specific interventions. Numerical values in the accuracy plots are figure-only; the text describes their trends.
record.test_reason: The study measures memorization of label-independent input backgrounds while retaining informative core features and true labels. It does not test random-label fitting, training on wholly unstructured inputs, label-corruption curves, regularization effects, or learning order. Interpolation in its RF/NTK analysis does not establish these versions for standard deep networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors characterize spurious-feature memorization through stability and feature alignment, derive RF/NTK alignment results that expose activation dependence, and report experiments supporting transfer to image datasets and networks capable of feature learning.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes spurious-feature memorization using theoretical random-feature and NTK regression models and experiments with added noise backgrounds; it does not use the original random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported spurious accuracy changes with training-set size, the fraction of input occupied by the spurious feature, activation function, and model feature map.

fits_no_version.finding: RF and NTK experiments show decreasing spurious accuracy as training-set size increases, alongside improving test accuracy; activation choice and background fraction affect memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models trained on true labels can memorize irrelevant input features, with strength depending on generalization, feature alignment, and activation.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that fully connected, convolutional, and ResNet experiments display the same generalization–spurious-memorization interplay; individual plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization of irrelevant input backgrounds also occurs in networks capable of feature learning.

record.problems: Several neural-network experiment results are shown only in plots; the text does not report exact plotted values or separately describe the trends for each architecture panel. The theoretical conclusions rely on stated distributional and over-parameterization assumptions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or wholly Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: States are assessed against V1–V6; cannot_determine does not negate the reported spurious-feature effects. Figures 6 and 7 add related experiments but no results testing these versions. Kernel invertibility and arbitrary-label interpolation concern the regression framework, rather than an empirical test of the stated deep-network claims.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label training, training and test error, architecture and hyperparameter changes.
Training time and convergence as label corruption varies.
Training on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error as random-label corruption increases.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: RF model (5.1)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate test accuracy and accuracy when queried with a training sample's noise background, replacing other pixels with 0.

conditions.value: ϕ2 = h1 + h2 and ϕ4 = h1 + h4

rows.measure: Test accuracy and spurious accuracy versus number of training samples N
rows.value: As N increases, test accuracy increases and spurious accuracy decreases; spurious accuracy increases with α and with an activation function having dominant low-order Hermite coefficients. Numerical values: figure only.
rows.note: Trend is described in text; plotted numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: Spurious accuracy does not measure any listed version. The model width is k = 10^5, not 105.
